title: The Man Who Received Tomorrow's Newspaper
logline: A man reads his own obituary in tomorrow's paper, avoids the fire, and learns the edition only needs one name.

source.notes: Original story written for The Midnight Archive. No third-party text used. Revised v2 keeps the prophetic-newspaper premise but replaces the erasure montage with a single causal substitution rule.

narration.text: The fine print said: one name per fire.
His neighbour's heater. The one she'd asked him to fix.
She said the super would come.
Elias took the stairs. He did not look back.
From the hotel, he watched the smoke.
The next paper waited at the desk.
Same fire. Same hour. Different name.
She had gone in to warn him.
Elias spread the editions across the floor.
Every one had taken a name.
The paper wasn't predicting the future.
It was choosing who paid for it.

final_line: It was choosing who paid for it.
visual_style: Sodium amber and ash grey against deep teal-black; one hard practical per scene; 24mm wides, 50mm mediums, 100mm macro details; fine 16mm grain; the newspaper is the only clean white value.
content_notes: Speculative fiction. The newspaper is a fictional device, not a factual claim about prediction, archives or fire safety. The neighbour's heater is narrative cause, not advice.
